content:
The owner of the small Pomeranian, Vivi, who was killed, today posted on social media to mourn her. The owner said Vivi loved going out, walking twice a day. Yesterday, while walking at a pet park, a large dog about half a person's height suddenly rushed out and bit Vivi on the neck.

The owner recounted that they tried multiple methods at the time, including kicking the large dog, spraying water at its nose, and using treats to lure it away, but the large dog held onto Vivi with a death grip and would not let go. The owner said, "I screamed for help and am grateful to the kind passers-by who assisted, but facing a large dog weighing dozens of pounds with a death grip that wouldn't release, there was nothing anyone could do. I could only watch helplessly as my little dog lost her life."

Vivi died on the spot. The owner recounted that the large dog remained guarding Vivi's body until the police arrived and restrained it, after which the owner was able to retrieve the body. "I later learned that the vicious dog had also killed another small dog. From beginning to end, the owner of the large dog never appeared."

The owner said that facing the sudden tragic incident, the whole family is deeply grieved and has been unable to sleep all night. "Vivi was an exceptionally well-behaved and gentle little dog, and the little angel of our entire family. I really want to hold her again and kiss her. I can't believe she left us so suddenly." The owner uploaded the last video of Vivi before the incident, showing Vivi sitting in a stroller, being well-behaved and adorable in a shopping mall. The owner said, "Only by repeatedly watching her curious and cute appearance can I temporarily forget the horrifying scene."

The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) responded to media inquiries yesterday, stating that after inspection, the dog involved in the killing has a microchip and a valid dog licence. The Department will contact the dog owner based on the licence information and will investigate the incident. Prosecution will be initiated if there is sufficient evidence.

The AFCD pointed out that dog owners must always keep their dogs under proper control, including using a leash to securely restrain large dogs, to avoid causing nuisance or harm to other people or animals. According to the Rabies Ordinance, dogs must be kept on a leash or otherwise properly controlled when in public places, or in other places where it can reasonably be expected that the dog may wander into a public place. Offenders may be liable to a fine of HK$10,000.

FactWire is currently inquiring with the AFCD whether the dog owner has been contacted today, and is awaiting a response.
